direction: Evolve the `score_ruin_nodes` hook toward a stagnation-adaptive, capacity-aware ruin priority: base term = normalized worst-cost removal saving (removal_savings / route_dists contribution of the node's route), modulated by route slack utilization (demand vs capacity) and a deterministic pseudo-random jitter whose amplitude scales with `stagnation_ratio` and `iter_frac`, so the LNS alternates between greedy worst-node destruction early and diversified related-destroy later; keep the ruin-size schedule tied to iter_frac so late iterations widen the removed set.

operations.mechanism: KB entry method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 documents that the L3 score_ruin_nodes hook is the only evolved component (deterministic Regret-2 repair, intra_2opt and Record-to-Record acceptance are fixed), and that prior evolution of exactly this hook gave a small but highly significant gain (+0.12%, p<1e-8) over the Worst-Cost Removal control at 500 ms — so the hook, not the skeleton, is where headroom lies. method-cvrp-lns-shaw-regret motivates diversifying the destroy operator (Shaw relatedness / randomness) alongside worst-cost removal rather than using worst-cost alone. Since the budget is 500 ms and p50 first feasible is ~171 ms, the anytime curve is tight; therefore diversification must be gated on stagnation_ratio (only after the search stalls) to avoid wasting the strict deadline. All terms are computed from the hook's state-only signature (removal_savings, route_loads, capacity, route_dists, stagnation_ratio, iter_frac) with no oracle/instance-id information, keeping the interface scale-invariant and whitelist-safe; postprocess is forced to 'none'.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: For cvrp_ruin_recreate/v1 at a 500 ms budget, a ruin scoring hook that linearly blends node worst-cost removal saving (primary) with route slack/capacity-utilization and a stagnation_ratio-scaled deterministic jitter will lower total tour length versus a pure worst-cost-removal control (L3-ctrl), i.e. the LNS escapes local optima after stagnation without hurting the early anytime curve, because the jitter amplitude only grows once `stagnation_ratio` rises while `iter_frac` is still small enough to allow many further iterations.
